title: api-gateway: stabilize streaming proxy buffers and tighten routing/payload limits for OpenAI compatibility
author: Sofia Patel
release_notes: Stabilizes streaming proxy behavior under backpressure, reduces tail latency for long streaming responses, and tightens API gateway routing/payload limits to improve OpenAI compatibility. No user-facing breaking changes expected; rollout gated by canary autoscaling policy.
body: Summary: This PR adjusts the API gateway's streaming proxy and routing logic to address intermittent streaming stalls and compatibility issues observed when clients use OpenAI-style streaming and function calling with large descriptors. Motivation: In the last two weeks we observed a regression where long-lived streaming responses would stall under specific routing and proxy buffer conditions (seen in ENG-1724). Investigations showed that the proxy's write buffer sizing + routing fallbacks could cause partial frames to be held until larger batches were available, which breaks some OpenAI compatible SDKs expecting timely event frames. Changes in this PR: 1) Streaming proxy: implement adaptive write-flush thresholds (min/max frame flush intervals and byte thresholds) to avoid head-of-line blocking. 2) Buffering: reduce default per-connection buffer cap from 512KB to 256KB and add a tunable per-route override for high-throughput routes. 3) Routing rules: tighten route selection so that function/tool-calling requests with structured_output=true prefer low-latency nodes; add a policy tag `prefer_low_latency_for_structured_output`. 4) Payload limits: enforce a 2MB soft limit for OpenAI-compatible payloads (with graceful 413-style fallback and suggestion header) and keep a 8MB hard limit at the gateway. 5) Backpressure: add explicit EAGAIN handling path that signals upstream runtime to flush KV caches earlier. 6) OpenAI compatibility layer adjustments: ensure chunked/event-stream frames are forwarded as-is and add a shim that emits `data: [DONE]` when stream terminates to match client expectations. 7) Tests and canary: add integration tests for streaming with function calling and a canary rollout config. Checklist: - [x] Proxy adaptive flush implementation - [x] Routing policy and per-route tags - [x] Payload limit enforcement and graceful error response - [x] OpenAI compatibility shim for final DONE event - [x] Integration tests covering streaming + tool calls - [x] Docs update (console and API docs) - [x] Canary rollout config for Dedicated and Hosted Impact: This reduces occurrence of streaming stalls seen in canary clusters and reduces tail latency for >60s streams. For most customers there is no change; customers hitting the previous >512KB implicit buffering may see earlier 413 responses for oversized payloads and can increase per-route override if needed. Rollout plan: Gradual canary across regions with traffic-weight gating and observability alerts on stream stalls. Related: ENG-1724, ENG-1799, SUP-521.
